cases.name: pause-punctuation-first
cases.note: Too long by 150 ms: the punctuation pause gives all of it, centred in its run, before any intra-phrase pause changes.

cases.name: pause-punctuation-versus-phrase
cases.note: Two 300 ms pauses, one after "today," and one after "and": only the punctuation pause shortens.

cases.name: pause-at-floor
cases.note: A punctuation pause of exactly 150 ms is at its floor and is not shortened; the intra-phrase pause gives the time instead.

cases.name: pause-at-floor-lengthens
cases.note: The same 150 ms pause at its floor lengthens when the take is too short, punctuation first.

cases.name: pause-run-shorter-than-fade
cases.note: A 10 ms run is shorter than SEAM_FADE and is never edited: the take pads at its seams instead.

cases.name: pause-run-equal-to-fade
cases.note: A 20 ms run equals SEAM_FADE: its one join needs the whole run, so it has no room to lengthen and the take pads instead.

cases.name: pause-run-just-longer-than-fade
cases.note: A 30 ms run can lengthen by 10 ms (the run less SEAM_FADE); the rest pads.

cases.name: pause-longest-run
cases.note: A voiced breath splits a 400 ms gap into runs of 120 and 250 ms: the longer run is the pause, and its length decides its room.

cases.name: pause-longest-run-tie
cases.note: Two equal 150 ms runs around a breath: the earlier run is the pause.

cases.name: pause-threshold-above
cases.note: A frame at the binary32 level just above VOICED_FRAME is voiced: it splits the 400 ms gap into runs of 200 and 190 ms, and the earlier, longer run is the pause.

cases.name: pause-threshold-below
cases.note: A frame at the binary32 level just below VOICED_FRAME stays a pause frame, so the 400 ms run stays whole.

cases.name: pause-frames-from-asset-start
cases.note: At 22.05 kHz an envelope frame is jsRound(220.5) = 221 samples, counted from the paid asset's first sample rather than from the trim at sample 470: the run is frames 9 to 29, samples 1,989 to 6,630.

cases.name: pause-take-edges-are-not-pauses
cases.note: The lead and tail silence inside the trims is not an internal pause: a one-word take that is too long has nothing to shorten.

cases.name: punctuation-categories
cases.note: Tokens ending in an ellipsis (Po), a right guillemet (Pf), a closing parenthesis (Pe), a left double quote (Pi) and a percent sign (Po) are punctuation pauses; a dollar sign (Sc) and a digit (Nd) are not.

cases.name: limit-punctuation-floor
cases.note: The punctuation pause stops at PAUSE_FLOOR_PUNCT (150 ms = 6,615 frames); the intra-phrase pauses take the rest in proportion to their lengths (8,820 : 6,615).

cases.name: limit-phrase-floor
cases.note: Every pause stops at its floor (150, 60 and 60 ms) and the last 2,205 frames are borrowed: 2,400 source samples, 1,200 at each gap seam.

cases.name: limit-growth-max
cases.note: The punctuation pause grows by exactly PAUSE_GROWTH_MAX (11,025 frames) and the intra-phrase pauses take the rest, 2,520 and 1,890.

cases.name: limit-growth-run
cases.note: The intra-phrase pauses grow only by their runs less SEAM_FADE (7,938 and 5,733 frames), and the rest pads equally at the two gap seams.

cases.name: limit-pad-gap
cases.note: Each gap seam pads at most SEAM_PAD_MAX (300 ms = 13,230 frames); 441 frames remain and the duration changes.

cases.name: limit-pad-hard
cases.note: Each hard seam pads at most HARD_SEAM_PAD_MAX (60 ms = 2,646 frames).

cases.name: limit-pad-edge
cases.note: A take edge pads at most SEAM_PAD_MAX beyond its edge pad: 16,317 + 13,230 frames at the take start.

cases.name: limit-borrow-slack
cases.note: Borrowing keeps PAUSE_SLACK_KEEP (7,200 samples at 48 kHz) beside each kept word: 0.4 s and 0.2 s of outside silence lend 12,000 and 2,400 samples, and the duration changes.

cases.name: redistribute-punctuation
cases.note: Punctuation pauses of 400 and 200 ms share 300 ms as 200 : 100; the shorter one stops at its floor after 50 ms, and the longer one takes the remaining 250 ms.

cases.name: redistribute-to-phrase
cases.note: With the punctuation pause at its floor, the last 100 frames go to the intra-phrase pauses: shares of 57.1 and 42.9 give 57 and 42, and the frame left over goes to the larger remainder.

cases.name: redistribute-tie-earlier
cases.note: Three equal punctuation pauses share 4 frames: each takes one, and the frame left over goes to the earliest of the equal remainders.

cases.name: redistribute-largest-remainder
cases.note: Pauses of 300, 200 and 100 ms share 7 frames: shares 3.5, 2.33 and 1.17 give 3, 2 and 1, and the frame left over goes to the largest remainder (the first pause).

cases.name: redistribute-together
cases.note: Two 200 ms punctuation pauses pass their 50 ms rooms in the same round and both stop at their floors; the 1 s pause takes the rest.

cases.name: seam-borrow-both-gaps
cases.note: With no pause, the residual is borrowed equally at the two gap seams.

cases.name: seam-borrow-odd-sample
cases.note: An odd number of borrowed samples puts the extra sample at the incoming seam.

cases.name: seam-borrow-passes-to-other
cases.note: The incoming gap lends only 441 samples (0.16 s less PAUSE_SLACK_KEEP), so it passes the rest of its half to the outgoing seam.

cases.name: seam-borrow-hard-incoming
cases.note: A hard seam has no gap to borrow from: the outgoing gap lends everything.

cases.name: seam-borrow-none-incoming
cases.note: A take edge has no outside silence to borrow: the outgoing gap lends everything, and the edge pad stays.

cases.name: seam-silence-within-slack
cases.note: Outside silences of 0.1 and 0.15 s hold no more than PAUSE_SLACK_KEEP, so nothing is borrowed and the duration changes.

cases.name: seam-pad-both-gaps
cases.note: With no pause, a short take pads equally at the two gap seams.

cases.name: seam-pad-odd-frame
cases.note: An odd number of padded frames puts the extra frame at the incoming seam.

cases.name: seam-pad-hard-passes
cases.note: A hard incoming seam stops at HARD_SEAM_PAD_MAX (2,646 frames) and passes the rest of its half to the outgoing gap seam.

cases.name: seam-pad-gap-to-hard
cases.note: A hard outgoing seam stops at its limit and passes the rest to the incoming gap seam.

cases.name: seam-times-off-grid
cases.note: A hard seam and the take end may lie off the sample grid, as section 8.4 places them. The planner returns both times on the source grid, even without borrowing.

cases.name: seam-times-borrowed
cases.note: A gap seam that borrows moves by whole source samples, and its time becomes the new sample over the source rate; the hard seam also returns its sample-grid time.

cases.name: edge-start
cases.note: At the take start the edge pad keeps the first aligned word 0.4 s from the edge, as in the source: 17,640 frames less the take's own 1,323-frame lead.

cases.name: edge-end
cases.note: At the take end the edge pad keeps the last aligned word 0.5 s from the end.

cases.name: edge-both
cases.note: A window over the whole take has an edge pad at each end, and e is their sum. A take too short for its pauses pads equally beyond both edge pads.

cases.name: edge-never-negative
cases.note: The source word starts only 10 ms after the take start, nearer than the take's 30 ms lead: the edge pad is 0, never negative.

cases.name: edge-pads-beyond
cases.note: A short take at both edges pads up to SEAM_PAD_MAX at each edge beyond its edge pad.

cases.name: edge-too-long
cases.note: A long take at the take start keeps its edge pad and shortens its pauses; the take edge lends nothing.

cases.name: changed-longer
cases.note: Too long beyond every pause floor between hard seams: every edit stays at its limit and the positive residual changes the duration.

cases.name: changed-shorter
cases.note: Too short beyond every growth limit and hard-seam pad: the negative residual changes the duration.

cases.name: changed-borrow-at-limit
cases.note: Pauses at their floors and both gap seams at PAUSE_SLACK_KEEP: the window widens by every borrowed sample and the take is still longer.

cases.name: round-tie-window-longer
cases.note: A 22.05 kHz take in a 44.1 kHz window of an odd sample count: n x 0.5 ends in .5 and rounds up to the take's own length, so the take fits exactly between hard seams. Rounding down would leave it one frame too long, with nothing to absorb it.

cases.name: round-tie-window-shorter
cases.note: The same tie one frame higher: the window holds one frame more than the take, which pads it at the incoming seam. Rounding down would leave the take unpadded.

cases.name: round-tie-borrow
cases.note: A 48 kHz take in a 44.1 kHz window must borrow 240 frames: 240 x 44,100 / 48,000 = 220.5 rounds up to 221 samples, 111 incoming and 110 outgoing (round-half-even would give 220).

cases.name: round-tie-edge-pad
cases.note: A 0.25 s source edge silence at 22.05 kHz is 5,512.5 frames and rounds up to 5,513; less the take's 661-frame lead, the edge pad is 4,852 frames.

cases.name: round-tie-growth-22050
cases.note: At 22.05 kHz PAUSE_GROWTH_MAX is jsRound(5,512.5) = 5,513 frames: a 27-frame run (5,967 samples) grows by exactly 5,513, and the hard seams pad the rest.

cases.name: round-tie-punctuation-floor-22050
cases.note: At 22.05 kHz PAUSE_FLOOR_PUNCT is 0.15 x 22,050, which is 3,307.5 in binary64 and rounds up to 3,308 frames: a 20-frame run (4,420 samples) shortens by 1,112.

cases.name: residual-incoming-pad
cases.note: Borrowing leaves the output one frame short of jsRound(n x 48,000 / 44,100): the frame pads the incoming gap seam.

cases.name: residual-incoming-edge-pad
cases.note: The output is one frame long: the incoming take-edge pad gives it up.

cases.name: residual-outgoing-pad
cases.note: A hard incoming seam takes no residual: the frame pads the outgoing gap.

cases.name: residual-outgoing-edge-pad
cases.note: The output is one frame long and the incoming gap pad is empty: the outgoing take-edge pad gives it up.

cases.name: residual-tail-trim
cases.note: The output is one frame long and no pad can shrink: the TTS tail trim ends one frame earlier.

cases.name: residual-lead-trim
cases.note: The tail trim already ends at the last aligned character: the TTS lead trim starts one frame later instead.

cases.name: residual-unplaced
cases.note: The aligned words fill both trims and no pad can shrink, so no pad or trim can take the residual frame. The incoming gap borrows the fewest more source samples whose widened window holds the planned frames, and the plan stays exact.

cases.name: residual-raise-outgoing-borrow
cases.note: The same with a hard incoming seam, as a 44.1 kHz take in a 48 kHz source: the outgoing gap borrows one more source sample, and the plan stays exact.

cases.name: residual-zero-borrow
cases.note: A 48 kHz asset in a 16 kHz source leaves one frame after pauses. The first borrow rounds to zero and neither trim can shrink, so the incoming gap borrows one sample and pads two frames.

cases.name: refuse-word-below-source-sample
cases.note: An aligned word shorter than one source sample is refused before fitting, even when the take has ample trailing silence.

cases.name: refuse-word-straddles-source-sample
cases.note: A 0.71-source-sample middle word straddles a source sample boundary after its offset. Only the input span rule refuses it, not the later output sample check.

cases.name: refuse-empty-word-text
cases.note: Aligned word text must be nonempty even when its patch token is not empty.

cases.name: refuse-final-word-clamp-collapse
cases.note: A final word inside the last half asset frame would clamp to an empty span at the output boundary. It is invalid timing, not a planner fault.

cases.name: round-unity-recipe-half-frame
cases.note: An odd 48 kHz source window rounds up at half a 24 kHz asset frame. Its unity recipe trims bound the output frames, not outDuration times an approximate stretch ratio.

cases.name: changed-offgrid-hard-residual-eight
cases.note: An off-grid 44.1 kHz hard/hard window with eight 24 kHz residual frames returns both seams on the source grid before computing its output duration.

cases.name: round-word-end-clamped
cases.note: A 16 kHz take in a 48 kHz source with both trims on its one word and no outgoing pad: the output holds jsRound(n / 3) frames, up to a third of a frame more than the window, so the word would end after windowEnd - windowStart. Its end is clamped to that duration.

cases.name: rates-22050-in-8000
cases.note: The sentence as a 22.05 kHz take in a 8 kHz source, 50 ms longer than its pauses can absorb: the pauses reach their floors and both gap seams borrow.

cases.name: rates-22050-in-16000
cases.note: The sentence as a 22.05 kHz take in a 16 kHz source, 50 ms longer than its pauses can absorb: the pauses reach their floors and both gap seams borrow.

cases.name: rates-22050-in-22050
cases.note: The sentence as a 22.05 kHz take in a 22.05 kHz source, 50 ms longer than its pauses can absorb: the pauses reach their floors and both gap seams borrow.

cases.name: rates-22050-in-44100
cases.note: The sentence as a 22.05 kHz take in a 44.1 kHz source, 50 ms longer than its pauses can absorb: the pauses reach their floors and both gap seams borrow.

cases.name: rates-22050-in-48000
cases.note: The sentence as a 22.05 kHz take in a 48 kHz source, 50 ms longer than its pauses can absorb: the pauses reach their floors and both gap seams borrow.

cases.name: rates-44100-in-8000
cases.note: The sentence as a 44.1 kHz take in a 8 kHz source, 50 ms longer than its pauses can absorb: the pauses reach their floors and both gap seams borrow.

cases.name: rates-44100-in-16000
cases.note: The sentence as a 44.1 kHz take in a 16 kHz source, 50 ms longer than its pauses can absorb: the pauses reach their floors and both gap seams borrow.

cases.name: rates-44100-in-22050
cases.note: The sentence as a 44.1 kHz take in a 22.05 kHz source, 50 ms longer than its pauses can absorb: the pauses reach their floors and both gap seams borrow.

cases.name: rates-44100-in-44100
cases.note: The sentence as a 44.1 kHz take in a 44.1 kHz source, 50 ms longer than its pauses can absorb: the pauses reach their floors and both gap seams borrow.

cases.name: rates-44100-in-48000
cases.note: The sentence as a 44.1 kHz take in a 48 kHz source, 50 ms longer than its pauses can absorb: the pauses reach their floors and both gap seams borrow.

cases.name: rates-48000-in-8000
cases.note: The sentence as a 48 kHz take in a 8 kHz source, 50 ms longer than its pauses can absorb: the pauses reach their floors and both gap seams borrow.

cases.name: rates-48000-in-16000
cases.note: The sentence as a 48 kHz take in a 16 kHz source, 50 ms longer than its pauses can absorb: the pauses reach their floors and both gap seams borrow.

cases.name: rates-48000-in-22050
cases.note: The sentence as a 48 kHz take in a 22.05 kHz source, 50 ms longer than its pauses can absorb: the pauses reach their floors and both gap seams borrow.

cases.name: rates-48000-in-44100
cases.note: The sentence as a 48 kHz take in a 44.1 kHz source, 50 ms longer than its pauses can absorb: the pauses reach their floors and both gap seams borrow.

cases.name: rates-48000-in-48000
cases.note: The sentence as a 48 kHz take in a 48 kHz source, 50 ms longer than its pauses can absorb: the pauses reach their floors and both gap seams borrow.

cases.name: s15-five-percent-longer
cases.note: D = 1.05 x w: the punctuation pause gives the residual above its floor, the take fits exactly, and every word keeps its aligned duration.

cases.name: s15-five-percent-shorter
cases.note: D = 0.95 x w: the pause lengthens by PAUSE_GROWTH_MAX and the rest pads equally at the two gap seams.

cases.name: s15-one-word-hard-seams
cases.note: A one-word take shorter than its window between hard seams pads HARD_SEAM_PAD_MAX at each, and the rest changes the duration.

cases.name: s15-borrow-beside-pause
cases.note: D = 1.15 x w beside a 0.6 s source pause whose seam leaves 0.55 s outside the window: the take's pauses reach their floors, then the outgoing gap lends the rest and keeps PAUSE_SLACK_KEEP beside the kept word.

cases.name: s15-forty-percent-longer
cases.note: D = 1.4 x w with no pause and no seam silence: changedDuration with no edit and residualSeconds = 0.4 x w (16,128 of 40,320 frames).

cases.name: s15-partial-at-limits
cases.note: Pauses and seams hold only part of the residual: every edit is at its limit and the window plus residualSeconds is the output.

cases.name: s15-take-edge
cases.note: At a take edge the pad keeps the first aligned word at its source distance (0.25 s) from the edge, while the pauses absorb a 5% longer take.

cases.name: refuse-synth-to-synth
cases.note: The planner places only none, gap and hard seams.

cases.name: refuse-gap-without-silence
cases.note: A gap seam needs its outside silence.

cases.name: refuse-hard-with-silence
cases.note: A hard seam has no outside silence.

cases.name: refuse-negative-silence
cases.note: An outside silence is never negative.

cases.name: refuse-take-start-off-zero
cases.note: A take-start seam lies on source sample 0.

cases.name: refuse-silence-before-take
cases.note: The incoming gap's outside silence cannot reach before the take start.

cases.name: refuse-empty-window
cases.note: The window holds at least one source sample.

cases.name: refuse-envelope-rate
cases.note: The envelope is on the paid asset's sample rate.

cases.name: refuse-envelope-length
cases.note: The envelope holds every whole 10 ms frame of the paid asset.

cases.name: refuse-asset-too-long
cases.note: A paid asset of 2^31 frames or more is refused before its envelope is read.

cases.name: refuse-trim-outside-asset
cases.note: The trims lie inside the paid asset.

cases.name: refuse-trim-end-before-start
cases.note: The trims are in order, checked in seconds before either is converted to frames, so a tail trim far below zero is refused rather than overflowing.

cases.name: refuse-source-rate-too-low
cases.note: The source rate is at least 1 Hz, the schema's floor.

cases.name: refuse-source-rate-too-high
cases.note: The source rate is at most 1 MHz, so no borrowed sample count overflows 64 bits.

cases.name: refuse-no-words
cases.note: A take without aligned words cannot be fitted.

cases.name: refuse-token-count
cases.note: Each aligned word has its patch token.

cases.name: refuse-empty-token
cases.note: A patch token is never empty.

cases.name: refuse-word-before-trim
cases.note: Every aligned word lies inside the trims.

cases.name: refuse-words-overlap
cases.note: Aligned words are in order and do not overlap.

cases.name: refuse-empty-word
cases.note: An aligned word ends after it starts.
